statement: StewardshipAssignments promised a 90-day review cadence for close-v1.1.0 and 60 days for policy-v1.0.0. Both the promise and the actual review history were in the model and nothing compared them, so a lapsed cadence was invisible.
resolution_plan: Resolved by ReviewEvents.ExceedsPromisedCadence and PromiseAndBehaviorDisagree, which compare DaysSinceReviewed against the cadence promised by the version's stewardship assignment. Surfacing the real Q1 review (review-close-q1) showed the witness firing on genuine history: 121 days elapsed against a 90-day promise. The Q2 review closed the lapse, so current state reads compliant.

statement: No validated fallback exists for simultaneous ERP and signed-snapshot repository outage.
resolution_plan: Resolved by adding offline signed export escrow.

statement: req-close-separation stated the preparer may not be the final approver, but nothing evaluated it. The control existed only as prose in a Requirements row, so a violation would have been invisible.
resolution_plan: Resolved by StepExecutions.ViolatesSeparationOfDuties, which counts preparation steps in the same procedure execution performed by the agent now approving. Verified by staging a breach (maria-chen approving se-close05 after preparing se-close03): the witness read TRUE. The staged breach was reverted; the control now reads FALSE because separation genuinely holds, not because nothing is checking.

statement: comm-sms-policy set ConsentRequired=true and exc-no-sms-consent documented the suppress-and-email handling, but no per-recipient delivery record existed, so a send to a non-consenting recipient was structurally invisible. req-policy-consent was a blocking control with zero satisfaction records.
resolution_plan: Resolved by the Recipients and MessageDeliveries tables plus MessageDeliveries.IsConsentViolation. Proven on md-003, a real SMS to a never-consented recipient, which the witness flags while correctly NOT flagging md-004 (consent revoked, properly suppressed under exc-no-sms-consent) or md-006 (unreachable, failed, HR case opened). Recipient re-consented; the delivery row is retained as evidence.

statement: SMS provider delivery receipts are not always final for ported numbers.
comm-sms-policy defined a 20:00-08:00 quiet window and nothing compared a send time against it.
resolution_plan: Resolved by MessageDeliveries.IsInsideQuietWindow and IsQuietHoursViolation, proven on md-005 (21:00 send). QuietHoursStartHour is stored rather than parsed: VALUE(LEFT("20:00",2)) does not translate — the transpiler casts the string to a timestamp and the view errors.

statement: MessageTemplates carried Status="Approved" as a bare string with no approval record behind it, and nothing evaluated a send BEFORE transmission. Every gate the communication policies define — consent, quiet hours, length, opt-out, approval — was checkable only after the fact, if at all.
resolution_plan: Resolved by the SendIntents table and IsClearedToSend, which gates a proposed send on permission, timing, content, and authorization before it happens, and names the blocking gate. Proven across seven intents: Timing blocks a 21:00 send, Content blocks an oversized body and one missing the STOP phrase, Permission blocks an unreachable recipient. Authorization blocked ALL sends until tmpl-policy-sms received a real approval record (tap-sms-001) — the pipeline had been transmitting under a template nobody had attributably approved.

statement: Five of twelve roles were held only by a denormalized Roles.CurrentAgent pointer with no RoleAssignments row: communications-manager, knowledge-authority, process-steward, close-automation, policy-drafting-agent. The convenience pointer claimed a holder the auditable time-bounded table could not confirm, so provenance for anything those roles touched was unverifiable.
resolution_plan: Surfaced by Agents.IsStillEngaged, which counts CURRENT RoleAssignments rather than trusting Roles.CurrentAgent. amina-yusuf read as not engaged, which made kf-policy-channel an IsUndefendableTacitClaim. Resolved by recording the five missing time-bounded assignments. The witness stays: it is the only thing that distinguishes a real appointment from a denormalized pointer.
